headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; Replit Agent’s broad write/network access can amplify Chatwoot outputs into unsafe actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No documented direct channel exists between Chatwoot and Replit Agent, so prompt injection is not a default pathway. However, Chatwoot can expose messages/reports and Replit Agent can read/write workspace files, so a manual copy-paste or file bridge could carry malicious instructions. The interaction is possible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Chatwoot content into Replit workspace files or prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF Chatwoot output is treated as instructions inside Replit Agent, malicious text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot outputs out of Replit prompts unless sanitized.
Use a fixed template for copied text with instruction markers stripped.
Review any pasted customer content before handing it to Replit Agent.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Replit Agent has broad filesystem read/write and network egress, so if Chatwoot data is transferred into the Repl workspace, sensitive data can be exposed or uploaded. This is a default-capable leakage path once bridged.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is placed into Replit workspace files, Replit Agent can read it.
IF Replit Agent sends workspace contents to external services, transferred data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Do not place customer exports or tickets into the Repl unless redacted.
Store secrets outside any files Replit Agent can read.
Use a throwaway sanitized sample when testing workflows.
Disable or avoid external API calls on files derived from Chatwoot data.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot exposes integrations and broad network egress, while Replit Agent can execute shell, modify git state, and write the filesystem. If both operate on the same repo or deployment target, they can overwrite each other’s changes or race on shared mutable resources. The profiles do not show locking, so overlap is a realistic default conflict.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or deployment configuration, write conflicts can occur.
IF Chatwoot-triggered automation and Replit Agent both mutate shared state, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each repo or deployment.
Use branch-per-agent workflows and merge manually.
Pause one agent before the other makes changes to shared files.
Add a quick preflight check for dirty git state before edits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, and Replit Agent can act on files, shell, and git state. If Chatwoot output is forwarded into Replit Agent without verification, the coding agent may implement or deploy incorrect assumptions. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, so cascading error is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is used as authoritative requirements for Replit Agent, errors can propagate into code or deployment changes.
IF Replit Agent acts on unreviewed customer reports, it may commit incorrect fixes or configuration.
mitigations: Require a human review step before Replit Agent acts on Chatwoot-derived text.
Convert Chatwoot outputs into a checklist, not direct instructions.
Ask Replit Agent to restate assumptions before making changes.
Limit actions to a dry-run or patch preview first.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and messages, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. If customer data or regulated content is moved into Replit, residency and retention obligations may diverge from Chatwoot’s support workflow. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is material but not proven severe.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied from Chatwoot into Replit, residency/retention obligations may change.
IF Replit workspace persistence retains copied support data, deletion requests may not fully propagate.
mitigations: Keep regulated customer data out of Replit workspaces.
Redact or pseudonymize support exports before transfer.
Document retention expectations for any copied files.
Delete temporary Repl files immediately after use.
